I am 53 years old, and I have been farming these lands in Quzhou County since I was a young man. My family has about 7 mu of good flat land on the North China Plain. I did not go far in school — only primary — but I know this soil and this climate better than any book. Every year for decades, I have grown winter wheat followed by summer maize in rotation, and that is what I will do again this year. I plant improved wheat varieties like Shimai or Lumai in October, and after harvesting in early June, I sow hybrid maize — Denghai or Nongda seeds — directly into the stubble without ploughing again, because that saves me diesel and time, and the crop still grows strong. I do rotary tillage before wheat sowing to break up the residue and level the field. For fertilizer, I spread compound fertilizer as basal dressing — around 100 jin per mu for wheat and 80–100 jin per mu for maize — and I topdress the wheat with urea at green-up to give it a boost. I irrigate from my well: three or four times for wheat, especially before winter and at jointing, and twice for maize, at seedling and tasseling. I also spray pesticides about four times on wheat and three times on maize, mixing insecticide, herbicide, and sometimes fungicide, because the bugs and weeds never rest. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu and around 1,100 jin of maize per mu if the weather holds. Cotton pays more per jin, but it needs spraying almost every week and my back is not what it used to be, so I will leave cotton to others and stick to grain.
